clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old man attacked by Asian giant hornets presented with difficulty breathing, headache, numbness, multiple sting marks, and initial low urine output. Initial labs showed leukocytosis and normal urine sediment. On day 3, serum creatinine was elevated indicating acute kidney injury. Over 10 days, oliguria worsened and creatinine rose significantly. Kidney biopsy on day 17 revealed normal glomeruli but tubular vacuolization and interstitial inflammation with eosinophils and lymphocytes confirming interstitial nephritis. Doppler ultrasound showed kidney swelling. Treatment with oral methylprednisolone led to improved urine output and decreased serum creatinine by day 31.
